problem:
Compute the standard deviation $\sigma $ of the following data set:

$$
15,\,1,\,-10,\,-13,\,-9
$$

Do not round your answer.

$\sigma =$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (15+1-10-13-9) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-16) \\  & =-\frac{16}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [{15}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-10)^{2}+(-13)^{2}+(-9)^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [225+1+100+169+81] \\  & =\frac{576}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{576}{5}-{(-\frac{16}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{576}{5}-\frac{256}{25} \\  & =\frac{2880-256}{25} \\  & =\frac{2624}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma  & =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2624}{25}} \\  & =\frac{8\sqrt{41}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
